title: The parser finds any code points other than ASCII whitespace or closing U+003E (>) after the DOCTYPE system identifier.
summary: The parser ignores these code points.

title: The parser finds a U+0022 ("), U+0027 ('), or U+003C (<) code point in an attribute name.
summary: The parser includes such code points in the attribute name.

title: The parser finds a U+0022 ("), U+0027 ('), U+003C (<), U+003D (=), or U+0060 (`) code point in an unquoted attribute value.
summary: The parser includes such code points in the attribute value.

title: The parser finds a U+003D (=) code point before an attribute name.
summary: In this case the parser treats U+003D (=) as the first code point of the attribute name.

title: The parser finds a U+0000 NULL code point in the input stream in certain positions.
summary: In general, such code points are either ignored or, for security reasons, replaced with a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.

title: The parser finds a U+002F (/) code point that is not a part of a quoted attribute value and not immediately followed by a U+003E (>) code point in a tag (e.g., <div / id="foo">).
summary: In this case the parser behaves as if it encountered ASCII whitespace.

title: The parser finds an ambiguous ampersand.
summary: In this case the parser doesn't resolve the character reference.
